findings.title: forEach callback made async but not awaited, breaking error handling and ordering
findings.body: The callback passed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(...)` was changed from a synchronous function to an `async` function so that `getCalendar` can be awaited inside it. However, `Array.prototype.forEach` never awaits the promises returned by its callback, so the surrounding `try { ... } catch (error) { logger.error(...) }` block (lines 124-139) no longer catches errors that occur inside the async callback (e.g. from `getCalendar` or `calendar.deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting`) — they become unhandled promise rejections instead. In addition, execution proceeds to the subsequent 'Send emails' step and the function's return without waiting for the calendar/video deletions to actually finish, so cancellations can race with (or occur after) the reschedule email being sent, and failures are silently swallowed instead of logged. Previously (sync callback + sync getCalendar) the try/catch correctly caught thrown errors synchronously. This should use `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered)` with awaited iterations, or `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => {...}))` awaited before continuing.

findings.title: forEach callback made async but not awaited, breaking error handling and ordering
findings.body: Identical issue to vital/lib/reschedule.ts: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => ...)` was changed to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` to allow `await getCalendar(...)`. Since `forEach` does not await the returned promises, the enclosing try/catch (lines 124-139) can no longer catch errors thrown inside the callback, they become unhandled rejections. The function also proceeds to send the reschedule email and return before the calendar/video deletions have resolved, introducing a race condition where the booking is reported as rescheduled/cancelled while the actual calendar/video cleanup may not have completed or may fail without being logged.

findings.title: forEach callback made async but not awaited in requestReschedule mutation
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => {...})` was changed to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` to allow `await getCalendar(...)`. `Array.prototype.forEach` ignores the promises returned by async callbacks, so this code fires off calendar/video deletion calls without waiting for them. The mutation then immediately proceeds to call `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` and send webhooks (lines 570-618) without any guarantee that the previous calendar event/video meeting has actually been deleted/updated, and any thrown error inside the callback becomes an unhandled promise rejection rather than being surfaced to the caller. This should use a for...of loop or `Promise.all` with `.map` so the async work is properly awaited before continuing.

findings.title: Dynamic import() calls execute eagerly at module load, not lazily on access
findings.body: `appStore` is an object literal whose property values are `import("./X")` calls. These dynamic import expressions are evaluated immediately when the object literal itself is evaluated (i.e. as soon as this module is loaded), not when a specific key such as `appStore.googlecalendar` is actually accessed. As a result, every consumer that imports `appStore` (getCalendar, videoClient, payment handlers, etc.) still triggers loading of all ~27 app sub-packages concurrently on every module load, rather than only the app that is actually needed for a given credential/booking. This does not provide selective/lazy loading of individual apps — it only converts previously-synchronous property access into asynchronous access (via `await appStore[key]`) while still eagerly fetching every app module. This may fail to deliver the performance/bundle-size benefit implied by the PR, while adding `await` boilerplate throughout many call sites.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now returns an unresolved Promise for `calendar`, risking silent breakage for other callers
findings.body: `getCalendarCredentials` calls `getCalendar(credential)` (now async) without awaiting it, so the `calendar` field in its returned objects changed from a resolved `Calendar | null` value to an un-awaited `Promise<Calendar | null>`. Within this file, `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to `await item.calendar` correctly, but `getCalendarCredentials` is an exported utility and this PR's file list does not show every consumer of it being updated. Any other caller that destructures `calendar` and does a truthiness check (e.g. `if (calendar) {...}`) will now always treat it as truthy because a Promise object is always truthy, silently breaking null-handling logic for credentials whose calendar service failed to initialize. This contract change should be verified against all call sites of `getCalendarCredentials`, not just the one touched in this diff.

findings.title: getVideoAdapters now resolves app lookups sequentially instead of in parallel
findings.body: The previous implementation built the adapters array synchronously via `Array.reduce`. The new implementation uses a `for...of` loop with `await appStore[appName]` inside, resolving each credential's app module one at a time instead of concurrently (e.g. via `Promise.all`). For callers that pass multiple credentials (e.g. `getBusyVideoTimes`), this serializes N dynamic-import resolutions where they could be run in parallel, adding unnecessary latency proportional to the number of credentials.

findings.title: No tests added for the new async appStore resolution / concurrency behavior
findings.body: This PR converts many previously-synchronous app-store lookups (getCalendar, getVideoAdapters, payment app resolution) into asynchronous ones and changes several forEach loops to async callbacks. None of the changed files include test updates verifying that calendar/video deletions during booking cancellation/reschedule actually complete before the function returns, or that errors from the now-async app lookups are still surfaced/logged correctly. Given the concurrency regressions introduced by the `forEach(async ...)` pattern in this PR, a regression test exercising cancellation/reschedule with a failing or slow calendar/video provider would have caught the issue.
